input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there

doc_friction.issue: Says to pick the project longest without a piece via git log, but on a shallow clone git log shows little; platform/ci/creative_due.py (named only in the hearth-and-horizon README) is the tool that actually works and should be linked from the prompt.

Step 0 has no rule for the case where every alert is claimed or already triaged as false; I had to read the triage report to see which unclaimed ones were known false. QUEUE.md could mark alerts already recorded in docs/reports as false positives.
The proposal names a 'churchwarden', an Anglican office; in a Catholic parish the finance committee chair is the realistic role, so the story adapted it.

deviations.why: Writeups default (a blog post with most PRs): the story is the reader-facing piece on a creative run, and a post would be a thin new post against the 2026-11-24 consolidation direction.
deviations.did: No post; the story and its closing model note are the write-up, and the security triage extended the existing agent doc.
deviations.result: Shipped the story plus the triage notes.

notes: Project: Hearth & Horizon, For Other Minds shelf (drawn by creative_due.py). Piece: the-step-that-had-three-falls-in-a-fortnight (text only; audio 581 MB > 400 MB cap). Numbers by Poisson formula and simulation (seed 20261125): fixed fortnight 1 in 584, winter-rate 1 in 172, sliding window 10.8%/yr, 68%/decade, 74% for 12 steps/yr; detection P(>=11|12)=0.65, P(>=19|18)=0.44. Weekdays checked with datetime. Added a new For Other Minds proposal (Chesterton's fence). Security step 0: unclaimed alerts #1049, #1050 (includes() check for a placeholder that must not remain, false positive), #1181-#1203 and #1208 (deliberate ReDoS test patterns and a vulnerable-repo fixture) recorded as false positives for owner dismissal. Verification: node --test in hearth-and-horizon 22/22; run_workflow_locally --for-changes 10/10 selected workflows passed, exit 5 no verdict for priv-codeql and priv-security-gate (CI is their verdict).

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a writer drafting and fact-checking a 3,900-word story with a simulated statistics model, plus an hour of security alert triage

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
